verified_primary_facts: The public CPO mask builder loads model.state_dict() and iterates every floating state-dict key that appears in both current and previous checkpoints; it does not canonicalize keys through duplicate-free named_parameters().
The public Qwen3-VL-4B GSPO mask launcher sets top_percent=10.0 and the run script binds the 4B path to Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct.
The official Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct config has tie_word_embeddings=true, vocab_size=151936 and hidden_size=2560, so the tied token/output matrix contains exactly 388,956,160 scalars.

For each state-dict key the builder independently allocates a dense bool tensor, and after union independently clones reference values under that same key before torch.save. There is no alias canonicalization or shared-output-storage reuse in this code path.

The trainer constructs _mask_flat_idx, n_tensors and n_pos from every serialized mask key before it iterates unwrapped.named_parameters() to inject gradients. Because default named_parameters() deduplicates a tied Parameter, an extra state-dict alias can inflate serialized mask/ref state and printed mask counts while not receiving a separate effective regularizer hook.

A source-equivalent local PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu fixture independently reproduced the mechanism: a tied Embedding/Linear pair appeared twice in state_dict but once in named_parameters; the two generated masks had distinct storage and the two cloned reference tensors had distinct storage.

Conditional on the alias key having at least one nonzero selected movement, its dense bool mask alone costs exactly 388,956,160 bytes = 0.36224365234375 GiB of raw tensor payload. If all requested 10% positions are nonzero, the alias adds 38,895,616 reference positions, making raw saved mask+float32-reference payload 544,538,624 bytes = 0.50714111328125 GiB and trainer-resident bool+float32-ref+int64-index auxiliary payload 855,703,552 bytes = 0.79693603515625 GiB.

The percentage summary can mathematically hide the alias duplication: when the duplicated tied key has the same selected-count fraction as its canonical key, adding that alias multiplies numerator and denominator by the same fraction contribution, leaving the reported selected percentage unchanged even though absolute n_pos, disk/RAM and build work increase.

scope_corrections.claim: The tied alias mask is guaranteed to be bitwise identical to the canonical mask across environments/runs.
scope_corrections.reason: The local fixture produced identical masks, but CPO calls torch.topk(..., sorted=False). PyTorch documents that indices of tied elements are not guaranteed stable and may vary across invocations. The storage/count duplication mechanism does not require bitwise-identical selected indices.

scope_corrections.claim: The worker's projected 8.764585% denominator inflation is fully independently verified here.
scope_corrections.reason: This audit independently verified the tied-matrix size and the alias mechanism, but did not independently reconstruct the worker's full-model physical parameter count 4,437,815,808 from the complete Qwen3-VL-4B checkpoint. The exact full-model denominator-inflation percentage therefore remains source-worker arithmetic pending full-model count binding.

scope_corrections.claim: The raw storage projections are measurements of the public CPO PyTorch-2.8/Qwen3-VL-4B training environment.
scope_corrections.reason: The executed fixture used local PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu and no real Qwen checkpoint. The byte calculations above are exact tensor-payload arithmetic conditional on support count, not measured task_k.pt archive size, RSS or wall clock in the paper/release environment.

scope_corrections.claim: The alias defect changed the published CPO paper-table quality numbers.
scope_corrections.reason: The public release exhibits the mechanism, but this audit does not bind the paper-table generation environment to this exact July-29 code path or measure quality impact on the released 4B tasks.

safe_to_use: Current public CPO mask-generation and trainer namespaces disagree on tied aliases: state_dict-side mask/ref construction can preserve a duplicate alias that named_parameters-side regularization does not consume as a separate parameter.

For Qwen3-VL-4B, any materialized dead tied-alias mask has a dense-bool lower-bound payload of about 0.362 GiB before reference/index storage; at full nonzero 10% support the exact raw payload calculations are about 0.507 GiB saved and 0.797 GiB trainer auxiliary state for that alias alone.
Selected-percentage logging is not a reliable detector of this alias duplication because duplicated numerator and denominator contributions can preserve the displayed fraction.
do_not_promote_without_more_evidence: Exact real task_k.pt archive-byte overhead, CPU/GPU RSS, build-time or per-step copy overhead without a pinned real-model run.
Bitwise equality of alias/canonical top-k masks across runs or devices.
The worker's full-model 8.764585% denominator inflation until the complete physical parameter count is independently bound.
Any claim that this release bug caused the paper's reported continual-learning quality differences.
